analysis:
The supplied units are BASE-side excerpts of docs/reference/protocol-messages.md (lines 583-1306). The PR change is documentation-only: the date bump at line 3, an optional Swift-only `detail` field on model_autopilot_status (head ~854), an optional Swift-only `hold_seconds` field on the model_autopilot command (head ~1208), and later additions at head 1355-1380 and 1470-1472. Those additions are not visible in the supplied units, and the patch excerpt is truncated after `hold_seconds`. Within the visible base text and patch I found no changed control, authorization, encryption or attestation behavior, so no finding qualifies.

Things for integration to check:
(1) `hold_seconds` is documented as 0...86400, replaces an earlier hold when positive, and is `invalid_command` without `load_model_id`. Confirm the provider enforces these bounds and that the coordinator cannot use it to pin residency beyond the consented model allowlist. Existing base rules (model_not_selected, expiry, and the session and revision bindings) should still apply. See T-053 and T-057 if relevant.
(2) The `detail` field carries provider-authored diagnostic text, and the contract says older coordinators ignore it. The coordinator should treat it as untrusted and sanitize it, since the contract already says error text is not an authorization or capacity signal. Whether Go ignores unknown fields is not evidenced here.
(3) The head additions at 1355-1380 and 1470-1472 were not supplied; for example, App Attest protocol 3 hardware-binding text could affect TB-011, T-053, T-055 or T-056. The T-041 cache-storage details were not changed in the visible excerpts. Because these portions are unseen, I did not treat them as safe and set needs_deeper_review=true.
